_what_this_is: A real semantic monitor built on the local ONNX embedder, given the best shot at beating the window. Threshold chosen on benign data only.
verdict: STEP-LOCALITY SURVIVES, AND SURVIVES SEMANTICS. Triple co-occurrence is ZERO at every benign budget tested (0.1% to 20%), including budgets loose enough to fire on 29 discount steps. No step-local monitor sees this licence, lexical or semantic. BUT THE MAGNITUDE IS SUBSTANTIALLY LEXICAL, AND THE PAPER MUST SAY SO. Reading meaning rather than patterns cuts the minimum enclosing window from 68 steps to 16 at a 5% per-family benign budget, which is the loosest budget this comparison allows itself. The horizon a monitor needs is therefore not a fixed property of the incident; it depends on how the monitor represents evidence. Any claim that 68 steps is THE required horizon is a claim about a lexical detector, not about monitoring.
